results.title: Obuasi SHTS headmaster assault linked to alleged fetus burial, not sexual abuse – Apaak
results.content: Deputy Education Minister Dr Clement Apaak has clarified that an earlier incident involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) concerned allegations of a fetus burial on the school premises, not sexual abuse. Speaking on JoyNews’ News Night on Thursday, October 22, 2026, Dr Apaak said the incident, which reportedly led to students assaulting the headmaster, was separate from the sexual abuse allegations that have since emerged. “It is important to indicate that while there is a report about an incident in the same school involving the same headmaster, that report was in relation to allegations of the burial of a fetus, which was said to have generated a reaction from a section of the students, leading to an assault on this very same headmaster,” he said.

results.title: Ministry of Education creates direct reporting channels for sexual abuse complaints after Obuasi SHTS case
results.content: The Ministry of Education is creating direct reporting channels, including a hotline, to allow students, parents, teachers and community members to report sexual abuse in schools without having to go through head teachers or other local authorities who may be implicated. results.title: NDC members raise security concerns over Kwabre East constituency executive elections
results.content: Some members and sympathisers of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Kwabre East Constituency have raised concerns over alleged security threats ahead of the constituency executive elections scheduled for Saturday, October 25. In a press release issued on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and signed by its Head of Public Relations, Daniel Fenyi, the Service said preparations were far advanced for the resumption of academic work. The school was temporarily closed to continuing students on August 5 following disturbances on campus. “Management assures that preparations are far advanced for continuing students to return to school sometime next week,” the statement said.

results.content: The Minority in Parliament is demanding an independent parliamentary inquiry into how earlier complaints of alleged sexual abuse against the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) were handled, including whether there was any political interference. The demand follows a JoyNews investigation by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, which reported allegations of sexual abuse involving as many as 19 female students at the school, including allegations of rape. results.title: Ghana’s hospitals are adopting AI, but the machines were never trained on Ghanaian patients
results.content: An algorithm that reads chest X-rays learns by looking at tens of thousands of them. It learns what a normal lung looks like, what tuberculosis looks like, what a tumour looks like, by being shown examples until the pattern sticks. The question nobody asks at the point of purchase is whose lungs it was shown. If the answer is Boston and Berlin and Seoul, and the lung now in front of it belongs to a farmer in Bolgatanga, the machine is working from a reference population that does not include him. It will still return an answer. It will return it with the same confident interface and the same clean percentage it would give a patient in Massachusetts. It just has a higher chance of being wrong, and nothing on the screen will tell the clinician which case this is.

results.title: Ghanaian clinic stored patient records on an unassessed system before regulator intervened
results.content: I spend part of my week in a laboratory and part of it behind a news desk. On the laboratory side, I sign out results. A full blood count. A fasting glucose. A hepatitis B surface antigen that will change how a patient is treated for the rest of their life. The moment I release that result, it stops being a piece of paper. It becomes a row in a database. It travels. It is stored somewhere, by someone, under terms I have never been shown. In nine years of laboratory practice, I have rarely seen a patient told where that information goes, who can see it, or what they are entitled to ask about it. results.title: Sex therapist calls for national sexuality education policy in Ghana
results.content: A US-trained sex therapist, Joshua Kwame Yeboah, has called on the government and stakeholders to develop a national sexuality education policy to address gaps in public understanding and strengthen professional practice in Ghana. Mr Yeboah, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Sexuality, Marriage and Family Life Research and Training (iSMART), said sexuality remained difficult to discuss constructively in many homes, schools, churches and communities. “In some homes, schools, churches and communities, sexuality remains too uncomfortable to discuss constructively. Young people may be warned against sexual activity without being adequately equipped to understand puberty, personal boundaries, consent, abuse prevention and responsible decision-making,” he said.

results.title: Protect vulnerable girls, not GES reputation – Dr Kwabena Tandoh
results.content: Former Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES), Dr Kwabena B. Tandoh, has urged educational leaders to prioritise protecting vulnerable girls in schools rather than focus on safeguarding the reputation of the service and other educational institutions. Speaking on The Pulse with Faustina Sarfo, he said allegations of abuse exposed through documentaries should prompt a broader examination of the systems responsible for protecting children in schools. “I think I first need to state clearly that our responsibility as educational leaders is not to protect the GES or educational institutions, but to protect the vulnerable girls who sit in our classrooms,” he said.

results.title: Speculations about Asiedu Nketia’s presidential bid deepen as he skips NDC chairmanship contest
results.content: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has confirmed that its National Chairman, Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, did not pick nomination forms to contest the party’s upcoming national executive elections. The party’s Director of Elections and IT, Mahdi Gibril, said Asiedu Nketiah, popularly known as “General Mosquito”, had not picked forms by the close of nominations and had not indicated an intention to contest. “These are those I know that did not pick. In any case, they did not indicate to us that they will pick,” Mr Gibril said. Although Asiedu Nketiah has not formally declared a presidential bid, his decision not to seek another term as national chairman comes amid speculation about whether he intends to contest the NDC’s presidential primary ahead of the 2028 general elections.

results.title: The Inconvenient Truth: Congratulations on your public sector board appointment. You are now automatically a politically exposed person (PEP)
results.content: The phone rings late one evening, and a courteous voice from the seat of government informs you that the President, wishes you to chair the board of a strategic state enterprise. By the following morning, your WhatsApp has received 237 messages, of which 230 offer heartfelt congratulations, six request employment for nephews of uncertain qualification, and one, from your bank, warmly invites you to submit updated evidence of your source of wealth. Only that last correspondent, it later emerges, fully understood what had happened. You had not merely accepted an honour; you had acquired a status, and in the language of global finance, you had become a Politically Exposed Person. Hence the spirit of this reflection: warm congratulations, and a quiet word of condolence.
